target.description: The column to predict. `dsbf.profile(target=...)` sets it; without one the check is not applicable.

n_neighbors.description: Neighbours of the estimator for a continuous feature or target; more smooth the estimate and bias it low.

min_normalised.description: Normalised mutual information from which a feature is reported, when it also exceeds the noise floor.

min_n.description: Complete rows a feature needs to be measured.

max_levels.description: Most levels a class column or target may have; the estimate over more is inflated by the levels' own noise.

max_rows.description: Most rows read; more are sampled with `seed`. The estimator searches neighbours, so its cost grows faster than the rows.

null_draws.description: Estimates against a shuffled target that set a noise floor, the highest of them: a truly independent feature passes it about once in `null_draws + 1`. A class feature gets that many of its own, since its estimate is biased up by its number of levels; the continuous features share one floor.

null_features.description: Continuous features measured against shuffled targets to set their shared noise floor.

null_shuffles.description: Shuffled copies of the target each of those features is measured against, or more when that leaves fewer than `null_draws` estimates.

seed.description: Seed of the row sample, shuffles and estimator.

max_findings.description: Most findings; the most informative first.

discrete.description: A class column, estimated from counts; else continuous.

mutual_information.description: Estimated mutual information with the target, in nats.

normalised.description: The share of the target's uncertainty the feature removes: for a class target its mutual information over the target's entropy; for a numeric one 1 - exp(-2 MI), which is r² for a bivariate normal pair.

n_used.description: Rows the estimate used: those where the feature and target exist.

noise_floor.description: The highest mutual information, in nats, this feature shows with a shuffled copy of the target.

notable.description: At least `min_normalised` and above the noise floor.

target_classes.description: Classes of a class target; None for a numeric one.

normalisation.description: `target_entropy` for a class target, `information_r2` for a numeric one.

features.description: Every feature that was measured, most informative first.

noise_floor.description: The highest noise floor, in nats, among the features of a kind (`discrete`, `continuous`): what a feature of that kind shows with a shuffled copy of the target.

untested.description: Features not measured, by reason: too_few_rows or no_variation.

skipped_columns.description: Columns left out, with the reason.
